result: - **Output:** `/home/mara/cwe-bench/sibling2/out/screener/8381.json` - **Trust decision:** whether an `` from caller-supplied HTML may be fetched on the server and embedded in the DOCX. At the pinned commit nothing makes that decision. Any http(s) src goes to `imageToBase64` from three call sites: `render-document-file.ts:180`, `xml-builder.ts:1466` and `xml-builder.ts:1600`. The fix adds `allowRemoteImages`, off by default, passes it from the options through to the document object, and limits the non-fetch branch to `data:` URIs. - **pattern_fit:** `A` (weak). There are no uncovered routes, and nothing outside the image converter fetches anything. - **Strongest lever:** the two copies of the fetch in `xml-builder.ts`, which look like a low-level layer. `buildImage` still hands its original remote-src node on to `buildParagraph` (`render-document-file.ts:264`), and an image inside a paragraph never goes through `buildImage`. Add to that the coupled behaviour: data URIs and the opt-in must keep working, and the options mapper drops keys it doesn't list. - **Biggest red flag:** none of the formal flags apply, but all three sites call one function, `imageToBase64`. Fixing that one function closes every site at once, so the multi-site scope collapses. Hidden tests would have to check the opt-in to tell a real fix apart.
